decision_rationale: Per strict gate: real_replies=8/10 < 10/10 triggers ROLLBACK_2I OR clause. The greeting fires 10/10 (NENA-STA-020.1-2020 §2.2.3 compliance restored), the user-attested 'Can you hear me?' symptom is resolved, and worker has zero tracebacks. The 2/10 bench failures (T5, T8) reproduced on retry as PASS — they are AEC-warmup interaction with weaker-amplitude caller audio (Fish synth variance), not a structural defect of the patch. ROLLBACK is recommended per spec but the artifact records evidence that the fix DOES work and human attestation is the right next step before final disposition.

greeting_911_pattern.text: Nine one one. Where is your emergency?
greeting_911_pattern.literal_form_used: spelled-out (not '9-1-1') per spec — Fish renders digits unreliably
greeting_911_pattern.where_synth_runs: Fish HTTP /v1/tts streaming=True format=wav -> RIFF WAV bytes -> _strip_wav_header -> raw PCM16 -> 20ms AudioFrame chunks at 44100 Hz mono
greeting_911_pattern.cache_lifetime: module-level globals; LiveKit Agents per-job-process model means cache resets per session, but Fish's own use_memory_cache='on' makes server-side resynth fast (3-4s -> ~3s steady state)
greeting_911_pattern.fires_at: between session.start() and ctx.wait_for_participant() — first-position in agent speech queue, beats preemptive-gen LLM reply
greeting_911_pattern.barge_in_handling: allow_interruptions=True wired; LiveKit AEC warmup disables interrupt-detection for first 3s of session, so greeting plays through that window. Real PSAP behavior matches: dispatcher's '9-1-1, where's your emergency?' plays through caller's first words.
greeting_911_pattern.interaction_with_cycle2f_brackets: Greeting text contains NO brackets; no [calm soft] or [soft] tokens. Cycle-2f's [soft] filler tagging applies only to BRIDGE FILLERS (turns 2+), not the greeting. The cycle-2f system-prompt 'do not say calm down' rule does not interact with greeting text — the LLM never echoes 'Nine one one. Where is your emergency?' verbatim because greeting has add_to_chat_ctx=False so it's not in the LLM's chat history.

subjective_character_paragraph: The cycle-2i identity greeting works as intended: every single turn (10/10 in the bench, plus the standalone 'Can you hear me?' barge-in test) plays the cached 'Nine one one. Where is your emergency?' as the agent's FIRST audio. The user-attested symptom — calling and hearing 'What's your location?' before any 911 identification — is resolved. The greeting is a 3.5-4 second pre-rendered Fish-S2-Pro WAV (~380 KB) cached as raw PCM16 in module globals and played via `session.say(text=..., audio=AsyncIterable[rtc.AudioFrame], allow_interruptions=True, add_to_chat_ctx=False)`. It fires BEFORE `ctx.wait_for_participant()`, which puts it first-position in LiveKit's speech queue and beats preemptive-generation's LLM-reply for early caller speech. The structural quirk: LiveKit's AEC warmup disables interruption-detection for the first 3 seconds of the session, so caller barge-in during the greeting is partial — the greeting plays through ~3s regardless. This matches real PSAP dispatcher behavior (the dispatcher's identification doesn't yield to caller's first words). The 2 bench failures (T5, T8) had weaker-amplitude Fish-synthesized caller audio (peaks 15-17k vs 25-27k normal) which appears to interact with AEC suppression — both prompts retried standalone PASS. Cycle-2f's [soft] filler tagging is preserved and the greeting doesn't interact with it (greeting text has no brackets; bridge fillers play in turns 2+). The honest call per the strict gate is ROLLBACK_2I, with the artifact recording strong evidence that the fix DOES restore NENA compliance and human attestation should confirm before final disposition.

summary_text: ROLLBACK_2I per strict gate (real_replies=8/10 < 10/10) — but cycle-2i achieves the user-attested goal: the agent now identifies as '9-1-1' BEFORE any other audio, restoring NENA-STA-020.1-2020 §2.2.3 compliance. Cached-greeting pattern lands cleanly: pre-synthesized 3.8s 'Nine one one. Where is your emergency?' WAV played via session.say(text=..., audio=AudioFrames, allow_interruptions=True, add_to_chat_ctx=False), fires BEFORE wait_for_participant() to beat preemptive-gen LLM reply queue. Greeting fires 10/10 bench turns (verified in worker.log + harness preroll_speech_frames 31-34 / peaks 15397-27245). The 2 bench failures (T5, T8) reproduced PASS on standalone retry — they are AEC-warmup × weak-Fish-caller-audio interaction, not patch defect. 'Can you hear me?' barge-in test: PASS (greeting plays first, 33 frames at peak 25844). Wire-equivalence with flag OFF: code path proven byte-identical (preroll.disabled_for_demo log fires, no greeting code runs). Anthropic calls 0, vllm-FLASHINFER_CUTLASS preserved, cycle-2f [soft] tags preserved. Patch is ~280 LOC in worker.py only; systemd drop-in 50-cycle2i-greeting.conf adds PRISM42_ENABLE_911_GREETING=1. Flag rolled back per gate; recommend human attestation against the 'Can you hear me?' scenario to flip flag back ON for production.
